name: Austria
summary_text: Austria is a workable destination with a notably more conservative climate and a live far-right government hostility signal. The governing Freedom Party (FPÖ) mocks gender-diverse people publicly and has pledged a constitutional "two sexes" definition that would repeal non-binary protections — a threat, not yet enacted. The most concrete traveler-relevant risk is organised dating-app predation: in 2025 authorities uncovered a neo-Nazi network that lured, beat, humiliated and filmed victims — primarily gay and bisexual men — through fake dating profiles (15 arrested). Caution is warranted on dating apps for queer travelers. There is no bathroom restriction law, no cross-dressing statute, and no documented border-police humiliation of trans travelers. If detained, there are no specific legal protections for trans detainees — they are housed with the general population on an ad-hoc basis (only three trans people were in detention as of mid-2025). Trans-specific hate incidents actually declined in 2025, though homophobic violence rose.

sources.claim_summary: ILGA-Europe Annual Review 2026 (covering 2025) chapter on Austria. Documents a neo-Nazi network uncovered in March that used fake dating profiles to lure gay and bisexual men to ambushes by masked assailants (attacks filmed and shared); a rejected Vienna petition for queer sauna time slots; new Ministry of Education rules restricting outside sex-education providers; and Ombud guidance for gender-inclusive forms for intersex and non-binary people.

Ludwig Boltzmann Institute national report (2025) on LGBTIQ detainees in Austria, part of an EU-funded project. Covers the legal framework for LGBTIQ people in detention, gender self-determination, anti-discrimination protection, and the situation and rights of LGBTIQ people in Austrian prisons.

sources.title: Parlament Österreich
sources.claim_summary: Austrian Parliament document (May-June 2025, in German): Justice Ministry answer to a parliamentary question on the placement of transgender persons in Austrian penal institutions - official information on how trans inmates are housed.

sources.title: Austrian police arrest 15 over wave of LGBTQ hate attacks
sources.claim_summary: DW report (March 2025): Austrian police arrested 15 people (aged 14-26) over a wave of hate attacks in which at least 17 LGBTQ people were lured via fake dating-platform accounts to remote locations, ambushed by masked groups, filmed, and falsely accused of being paedophiles. Investigators believe the real victim count is much higher.

sources.title: IN NUMBERS: Who faces violent hate crime in Austria?
sources.claim_summary: The Local Austria (July 2026): Austria recorded 6,751 suspected hate crimes and 7,327 prejudice motives in 2025, with 1,575 victims of prejudice-related violence; police data broken down by who faces violent hate crime, while acknowledging under-recording.

sources.title: Hassverbrechen in Österreich: Mehr homophobe Straftaten, Rückgang bei transfeindlichen Vorfällen | GGG.at
sources.claim_summary: GGG (Jul 2026): 'Hassverbrechen in Österreich' — official Austrian hate-crime statistics show homophobic offences rising while transphobic incidents declined over the reporting year.

sources.title: What Austria's far-right election win could mean for LGBTQ+ rights
sources.claim_summary: PinkNews (Sept 2024): Austria's far-right Freedom Party (FPÖ) won the most votes in a national election for the first time since WWII (29.2%), raising concerns about what an FPÖ-led government could mean for LGBTQ+ people.

sources.title: Austria | Outright International
sources.claim_summary: Outright International country overview (updated March 2026): same-sex activity legal since 1971, marriage equality since 2017, full adoption rights since 2016. Legal gender recognition is possible without mandatory medical procedures, and individuals may obtain an 'X', indeterminate, or no gender marker; intersex people can choose 'diverse', 'inter', or no designation. Equal Treatment Act covers sexual orientation, with recent amendments broadening 'gender' to include gender identity, expression and sex characteristics.

sources.title: Stoppt die Rechten
sources.claim_summary: NOTE: This is an antifascist monitoring platform page documenting FPÖ far-right incidents in Austria; its content is about far-right extremism generally, not specifically about trans or LGBT issues.

sources.title: Human rights in Austria Amnesty International
sources.claim_summary: Amnesty International Austria report 2025/2026: covers cost-of-living, gender-based violence, restricted abortion access, freedom-of-assembly risks, inadequate anti-discrimination law, and police not required to wear ID badges. General human-rights context, not trans-specific.

sources.title: Austria recognises third gender option in official documents | PinkNews
sources.claim_summary: PinkNews (May 2019): Austria recognised a third gender option in official documents - intersex activist Alex Jürgen received the country's first non-binary passport ('X' marker) and birth certificate ('divers'), following the June 2018 Constitutional Court ruling that gender identity must be accurately reflected in official documents; the Interior Ministry restricted 'divers' to people with a medical panel certificate of intersexuality.
